findings.title: CIMA AML/CFT/CPF Rule and Sanctions Rule In Force — No Transition Period
findings.summary: The CIMA AML/CFT/CPF Rule and Sanctions Rule entered legal force on 18 September 2026 with no transition period. The AML Rule converts previously advisory Guidance Notes into binding obligations for all CIMA-regulated entities (including registered investment funds), adding mandatory independent AML audits, written AMLCO outsourcing agreements, and enhanced ongoing effectiveness testing. The Sanctions Rule makes sanctions-screening directly enforceable by CIMA with civil fine authority.
findings.client_impact: HNW clients with Cayman-registered funds, SPVs, or managed accounts must confirm their fund boards can document AML/CFT programme compliance as of 18 September 2026 — CIMA can now levy fines for non-compliance with no grace period. Independent AML audit scheduling and AMLCO agreement reviews should be initiated immediately if not already underway.
findings.urgency_reason: Rule already in force as of 18 September 2026 with no transition period; exposure to CIMA penalties is current, not prospective.

findings.title: BCB Resolution 561: Stablecoin Settlement for eFX Providers Banned from 1 October 2026
findings.summary: BCB Resolution No. 561 (published 30 April 2026) takes effect 1 October 2026, prohibiting eFX providers from settling cross-border payments using stablecoins or crypto assets. USDT and USDC have been re-classified as Foreign Exchange Operations under Resolution 521. All cross-border settlements must route through formal FX channels with authorised counterparties only.
findings.client_impact: Brazilian HNW clients or family businesses using eFX providers that currently route cross-border remittances via stablecoins (USDT/USDC) have 10 days to migrate to BCB-authorised FX channels — continued stablecoin settlement after 1 October will constitute a regulatory violation. Advisers should urgently audit payment flows for affected clients.
findings.urgency_reason: Compliance deadline is 1 October 2026, ten days from today; no grandfathering for existing arrangements.

findings.title: Brazil VASP Licensing Transition Ends 29 October 2026 — Unlicensed Operators Must Cease
findings.summary: BCB Resolution 520's transition period for existing VASPs (virtual asset intermediaries, custodians, and brokers) expires 29 October 2026. Firms that have not secured BCB authorisation must cease virtual asset operations in Brazil. Capital requirements range from approximately R$10.8–37.2 million (USD 2.2–7.6 million). Foreign operators are included.
findings.client_impact: Wealth managers facilitating digital asset transactions for Brazilian clients through local intermediaries or custodians must immediately confirm whether those counterparties are licensed or have authorisation pending — using an unlicensed VASP after 29 October exposes clients and advisers to regulatory risk. Approximately 38 days remain to identify and switch to compliant providers.
findings.urgency_reason: Hard licensing deadline on 29 October 2026 leaves fewer than 40 days; due-diligence reviews of all Brazilian digital asset counterparties must begin immediately.

findings.title: OECD/G20 Inclusive Framework Releases September 2026 Pillar Two Package
findings.summary: On 11 September 2026 the OECD released a Pillar Two package comprising new Administrative Guidance (covering Explicitly Conditional Taxes and QDMTT Safe Harbour clarifications for mismatched fiscal periods), an updated GloBE Information Return (GIR) mandatory for fiscal years beginning on or after 31 December 2025, and a legislative peer review framework for domestic minimum top-up taxes. In-scope MNE groups should reassess Pillar Two governance and GIR reporting processes immediately.
findings.client_impact: HNW family groups with multinational corporate structures exceeding the EUR 750 million revenue threshold must update their Pillar Two governance frameworks and GIR processes to reflect the new Administrative Guidance — particularly those relying on QDMTT Safe Harbour assumptions under local GAAP or with Explicitly Conditional Tax positions that are now confirmed excluded from Covered Taxes.
findings.urgency_reason: Updated GIR is mandatory for FY 2025 onward; no immediate penalty deadline but non-compliance with revised GIR requirements creates filing-accuracy risk for in-scope groups.

findings.title: BDO and PwC Publish Client Alerts on OECD Pillar Two September 2026 Package
findings.summary: Major advisory firms confirmed that the revised GIR is now mandatory for FY2025+ filings, that Explicitly Conditional Taxes are excluded from Covered Taxes, and that the QDMTT Safe Harbour expressly accommodates entities using local GAAP under a different fiscal period. The legislative peer review framework sets detailed criteria regulators will use to evaluate whether domestic minimum taxes qualify as QDMTTs.
findings.client_impact: This advisory coverage provides concrete implementation guidance for family groups and corporate structures in FGC's client base that are in scope for Pillar Two; tax advisers should benchmark client QDMTT Safe Harbour analyses and covered-tax positions against the clarified standards before year-end 2025 GIR filings.
findings.urgency_reason: Supplementary advisory guidance on the 11 September OECD package; no new deadline beyond the GIR mandate, but confirms key technical positions that affect HNW clients' multinational holding structures.

findings.title: Maples Group and Walkers Publish Practical Implementation Guides for CIMA AML and Sanctions Rules
findings.summary: Maples Group and Walkers published updated implementation guides for funds on the CIMA AML Rule and Sanctions Rule (effective 18 September 2026). Key actions include: sanctions screening against all applicable lists pre-onboarding and periodically thereafter; independent AML audits covering programme effectiveness; written AMLCO outsourcing agreements with ongoing board supervision; and documented board minute-taking requirements. Both firms confirmed that AMLCO appointment or confirmation must be documented by the board.
findings.client_impact: For fund boards and their investment managers that have not yet reviewed the Maples and Walkers implementation checklists, these guides provide the step-by-step compliance roadmap needed to demonstrate conformance with the already-binding CIMA AML and Sanctions Rules — immediate review is recommended to close any gaps before CIMA examinations.
findings.urgency_reason: Classified WATCH rather than URGENT because this is implementation guidance for the URGENT CIMA rule (see above); the rule itself is the action trigger, and this finding provides the how-to framework.

findings.title: ADGM FSRA Finalises Enhanced Funds Framework — Effective 16 September 2026
findings.summary: ADGM's FSRA published the final enhanced framework for Fund Managers and Funds effective 16 September 2026, introducing proportionate requirements for sub-threshold managers, a new institutional-only fund manager category with lighter-touch obligations, and streamlined passporting for foreign fund managers from recognised jurisdictions. ADGM is now ahead of DIFC, which remains at consultation stage.
findings.client_impact: HNW clients or family offices considering UAE-based fund or investment structures should evaluate ADGM as the more commercially permissive jurisdiction given the new proportionate framework — particularly foreign managers from FATF-equivalent jurisdictions who can now passport in more easily — and should factor the ADGM advantage into any UAE structure selection made in the coming months.
findings.urgency_reason: Framework is effective now with no compliance deadline for existing structures; WATCH status reflects opportunity to assess ADGM as a structuring venue rather than an imminent obligation.

findings.title: FinCEN Final Rule Permanently Exempts All US-Formed Entities from CTA BOI Reporting
findings.summary: FinCEN's final rule (14 August 2026) permanently exempts all entities created in the United States and their beneficial owners from Corporate Transparency Act BOI reporting requirements. Previously submitted BOI data for US persons will be deleted. Only foreign reporting companies (approximately 28,000, down from 32.6 million) must now file; new deadlines apply to qualifying foreign entities.
findings.client_impact: HNW clients who maintain both US-domestic and foreign entities in their structures should immediately confirm which entities are now fully exempt (all US-formed LLCs, corporations, etc.) versus which remain subject to BOI filing as 'foreign reporting companies' — foreign entities registered to do business in the US that don't qualify for an exemption still face active filing obligations under the revised framework.
findings.urgency_reason: Major structural change already in force; no 30-day deadline but clients with foreign entities doing business in the US need to assess their filing status under the revised foreign reporting company definition before their next annual compliance review.

findings.title: Lei Complementar 227/2026 — ITCMD Now Applies to Foreign-Sited Assets for Brazilian Heirs
findings.summary: Signed January 2026, LC 227/2026 mandates progressive state ITCMD rates (2%–8%) replacing flat structures, and resolves the constitutional gap by requiring states to impose ITCMD on foreign-sited assets received by Brazilian-domiciled heirs (implementing STF RE 851.108). Most states expected to be fully compliant by mid-2027; the anterioridade principle may delay implementation in some.
findings.client_impact: Brazilian-resident beneficiaries of offshore trusts, foreign holding companies, and international investment accounts now face state inheritance tax on non-Brazilian assets — a fundamental change that requires immediate review of all existing succession and trust structures for clients with Brazilian-domiciled heirs, as the applicable tax rate, situs rules, and treaty positions must be reassessed.
findings.urgency_reason: No single 30-day compliance deadline, but state implementation is rolling in real time through mid-2027; planning changes (restructuring, trust amendments, gifting strategies) made now before a state's compliance date carry the greatest structural benefit.

findings.title: Brazil Proposed Wealth Tax (IGF) — PLP No. 5/2026 Moving Through Congress
findings.summary: PLP No. 5/2026 proposes an annual wealth tax (Imposto sobre Grandes Fortunas) on individuals with net worth exceeding R$10 million. Constitutionally authorised since 1988 but never enacted; this bill is now in initial Congressional phase. No effective date set; significant amendments expected.
findings.client_impact: Brazilian UHNW clients with net worth above R$10 million should be aware that a recurring annual wealth tax is under active legislative debate; while passage is not imminent, advisers should begin tracking the bill's progress and stress-testing client portfolios for scenarios with a 1–2% annual IGF to inform any pre-enactment restructuring options.
findings.urgency_reason: No effective date or binding deadline; classified WATCH because the bill is in active Congressional process and advisers to Brazilian UHNW clients need to monitor it closely for potential structuring implications.

findings.title: BVI Beneficial Ownership Register — Full Penalty Enforcement Operational Since 1 April 2026
findings.summary: The BVI BO Register reached full operability on 1 April 2026 following the penalty moratorium expiry on 31 March 2026. Legitimate interest access requests are now accepted. Entities that missed the 1 January 2026 filing deadline are marked 'In Penalty' on the BVI FSC system and face ongoing penalties.
findings.client_impact: HNW clients with BVI companies that have not filed or updated their BO Register entries are currently accruing penalties and may face suspension or strike-off; advisers should conduct an audit of BVI entity portfolios to identify any 'In Penalty' status entities and instruct registered agents to remediate immediately.
findings.urgency_reason: Penalty exposure is live and accumulating; classified WATCH rather than URGENT because there is no single future deadline — the ongoing penalty status means remediation should happen promptly but is not triggered by an imminent date.

findings.title: Luxembourg AIFMD II / UCITS VI Transposition Law Effective 16 April 2026
findings.summary: The Law of 3 March 2026 (Bill 8628) transposes AIFMD II and UCITS VI into Luxembourg law effective 16 April 2026, amending both the 2010 UCITS law and 2013 AIFM law. Changes include enhanced liquidity management tools, new loan-originating AIF rules, expanded delegation disclosures, and revised ManCo substance expectations. Reporting obligations apply from 16 April 2027.
findings.client_impact: HNW clients invested in Luxembourg AIFs or UCITS, or those using Luxembourg ManCos for fund structuring, should confirm that their managers are on track to comply with the new delegation disclosure requirements and liquidity management tools now in force, and that reporting systems will be ready for the April 2027 AIFMD II reporting deadline.
findings.urgency_reason: Law is already in force; reporting obligation deadline is April 2027, giving managers roughly six months to prepare — early-stage infrastructure changes needed now.

findings.title: Luxembourg Carried Interest Regime Enacted — Law of 22 January 2026, Retroactive to 1 January 2026
findings.summary: Luxembourg enacted a revised carried interest regime via Law of 22 January 2026, retroactive to 1 January 2026. The law provides a permanent statutory framework replacing prior administrative practice for taxation of carried interest received by qualifying fund managers and investment professionals through Luxembourg-domiciled entities.
findings.client_impact: Wealth managers and fund sponsors with carried interest or GP economic rights flowing through Luxembourg entities should review the new statutory conditions with Luxembourg counsel to confirm qualification and optimise the tax treatment of incentive compensation — the retroactive application to 1 January 2026 means structures in place this year are already governed by the new law.
findings.urgency_reason: No compliance deadline beyond the retroactive 1 January 2026 effective date; advisers should confirm the new statutory conditions are met in existing structures before the 2026 tax return filing season.

findings.title: FINMA Launches Consultation on Comprehensive AML Ordinance Update
findings.summary: FINMA has opened consultation on a comprehensive revision to the AML Ordinance (AMLO-FINMA) mandating identification of natural-person ultimate controllers regardless of offshore layering, stricter risk-based supervision benchmarks, and expanded beneficial ownership transparency. The revision follows FATF recommendations and aligns with the 2021 revised GwG.
findings.client_impact: HNW clients who use Swiss private banks or financial intermediaries should anticipate that enhanced UBO identification requirements — including look-through of multi-layer offshore structures — will require updated KYC documentation packages; advisers should begin preparing comprehensive BO identification files for structures that include opaque intermediary layers.
findings.urgency_reason: Consultation phase only; no effective date set, but the direction of travel is clear and structures that will struggle under the proposed standards should be identified and addressed during the consultation window.

findings.title: MAS Consults on Stablecoin Legislative Framework — Feedback Deadline 16 October 2026
findings.summary: MAS published a consultation paper on 1 September 2026 proposing a licensing regime for Singapore-incorporated single-currency stablecoin issuers and a recognition regime for qualifying foreign issuers. MAS would gain power to designate systemically significant stablecoins. Feedback due 16 October 2026.
findings.client_impact: Family offices and HNW clients using Singapore entities for treasury management or cross-border transfers denominated in SGD or G10 stablecoins should track this consultation, as its outcome will determine the regulatory status and compliance requirements for any stablecoin-based liquidity management within Singapore structures.
findings.urgency_reason: Consultation deadline is 16 October 2026 (25 days); no compliance obligation yet, but the outcome will directly regulate stablecoin use by Singapore-based wealth structures and clients should be aware before the framework is finalised.

findings.title: MAS Introduces Single-Class Exemption for Single Family Offices — Effective 15 June 2026
findings.summary: MAS replaced individual SFO licensing exemptions with a statutory class exemption effective 15 June 2026. A qualifying SFO meeting defined conditions (minimum AUM, qualifying family members, Singapore nexus) requires only annual notification and a short return — no individual exemption application or CMS licence. Establishment lead times reduced from months to weeks.
findings.client_impact: HNW families considering a Singapore family office structure can now establish and operate a qualifying SFO significantly more quickly and with lower regulatory overhead than before June 2026 — advisers should present this streamlined pathway when evaluating Singapore alongside other family office jurisdictions such as Hong Kong, ADGM, or the Cayman Islands.
findings.urgency_reason: No compliance deadline; classified WATCH as an important structural planning development that should be factored into any ongoing or upcoming Singapore SFO establishment conversations.

findings.title: Cyprus 2026 Tax Reform: Corporate Rate to 15%, SDC on Dividends Cut to 5%, DDD Abolished
findings.summary: Effective 1 January 2026: corporate income tax raised from 12.5% to 15% (Pillar Two alignment); Special Defence Contribution on dividends for Cyprus-tax-resident/domiciled individuals cut from 17% to 5% on 2026+ profits; deemed dividend distribution mechanism abolished; loss carry-forward extended to seven years.
findings.client_impact: HNW clients using Cyprus holding companies for treaty-network structuring must review whether the 2.5 percentage point corporate rate increase affects their cost-of-capital analysis and whether any treaty-based structure that relied on Cyprus's low tax rate as a principal purpose remains defensible under revised substance analyses — while the SDC reduction partially offsets the rate increase for dividend extraction, treaty eligibility and BEPS substance criteria are the primary concerns.
findings.urgency_reason: In force since 1 January 2026; no new deadline, but structures established or reviewed before the reform that relied on a 12.5% rate assumption require re-evaluation.

findings.title: CRS 2.0 Trade Testing Complete; UK Moving to Separate CRS/FATCA Schemas from 1 January 2027
findings.summary: The OECD's CRS 2.0 (applicable from January 2026) completed trade testing on 18 September 2026. The UK will cease its combined CRS/FATCA schema after 31 December 2026, moving to the OECD's amended CRS XML schema and the IRS FATCA schema separately. The OECD Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF) entered initial implementation across 48 jurisdictions from January 2026; first automatic CARF data exchange expected September 2027 for 2026 data.
findings.client_impact: HNW clients holding financial accounts in the UK or in CARF-implementing jurisdictions through offshore structures should be prepared for enhanced automatic information exchange beginning with 2026 data: CRS 2.0 closes known reporting gaps, and CARF will capture crypto-asset holdings that previously fell outside CRS reporting, increasing the visibility of offshore wealth to home-country tax authorities.
findings.urgency_reason: CARF and CRS 2.0 are operational now for 2026 data; UK schema change effective 31 December 2026 is a compliance deadline for reporting institutions — advisers should ensure client account structures are correctly documented under the new standards before year-end.

findings.title: Panama Economic Substance Law 526 of 2026 — Substance Requirements for Offshore Entities
findings.summary: Panama enacted Economic Substance Law 526 of 2026 requiring Panama companies engaged in holding, IP, distribution/service centre, headquarters, and shipping activities to demonstrate genuine economic substance in Panama. This adds to RUBF beneficial ownership registry requirements (Law 129/2020) and the private BO register (Law 52/2016).
findings.client_impact: HNW clients using Panama holding companies or Panama-based IP or shipping structures must now demonstrate real economic substance in Panama — absent genuine local management, employees, and operational expenses, existing structures face non-compliance risk and potential recharacterisation by foreign tax authorities referencing Panama's new substance law.
findings.urgency_reason: Law enacted in 2026 with ongoing compliance obligations; no single imminent deadline, but existing structures without substance must be restructured or wound down to avoid accumulating non-compliance exposure.

findings.title: Florida SB 264 Foreign Buyer Restrictions Fully in Force — No New Changes in 2026
findings.summary: Florida SB 264 (effective July 2023, upheld November 2025) continues to restrict or prohibit real estate purchases by nationals of seven 'countries of concern' — China, Russia, Iran, North Korea, Cuba, Venezuela, Syria. No amendments were enacted in the September 2026 legislative cycle; proposed modifications failed, leaving the 2023 restrictions unchanged.
findings.client_impact: HNW clients who are nationals or legal entities controlled from any of the seven listed countries remain subject to Florida real estate purchase restrictions and should not proceed with Florida acquisitions without prior legal review; no new planning changes are triggered by the September 2026 cycle, but advisers should maintain these restrictions as a standing screen in their real estate advisory workflow.
findings.urgency_reason: Status quo confirmed; no regulatory change and no new deadline. Background awareness for advisers with clients from affected nationalities.

findings.title: FIRPTA 15% Withholding Rate Confirmed for 2026; IRS IRM Updated January 2026
findings.summary: The standard FIRPTA withholding rate remains 15% of gross sales price for 2026. The IRS revised IRM section 3.22.261 effective 1 January 2026 updating compliance procedures. The $300,000 personal residence exemption and 10% reduced rate for sales below $1 million remain unchanged. Some US states added additional foreign ownership restrictions in 2025–2026.
findings.client_impact: Foreign HNW clients selling US real property interests in 2026 remain subject to the standard 15% FIRPTA withholding regime with no changes to rates or exemptions; advisers should note that several US states have layered additional restrictions or reporting requirements on top of FIRPTA and should check state-level rules for any pending transactions.
findings.urgency_reason: Status quo confirmed with no rate or threshold changes; flagged as FYI to confirm the baseline for current and pending real estate transactions.

findings.title: Bahamas AEOI (Amendment) Bill 2026 — CRS Nil Returns Now Mandatory
findings.summary: The AEOI (Amendment) Bill 2026 requires financial institutions with no reportable CRS accounts to submit nil returns. The Bahamas simultaneously enacted the Decentralised Autonomous Organisations Act 2026 and a Domestic Minimum Top-Up Tax aligned with Pillar Two.
findings.client_impact: Bahamian financial institutions servicing FGC clients' accounts or structures must now file CRS nil returns where previously they may have stayed silent — this improves CRS data completeness and may prompt additional queries from clients' home-country tax authorities expecting reporting from Bahamian institutions that have historically not reported.
findings.urgency_reason: Operational compliance for Bahamian institutions; no direct client action required for HNW individuals, though it signals Bahamas's continued AEOI alignment and should be factored into information-exchange risk assessments for Bahamas-based structures.

findings.title: MFSA Identifies Outsourcing Shortcomings in Fund Managers; Structural Reforms Under Act XV of 2026
findings.summary: The MFSA published September 2026 findings on inadequate outsourcing due diligence and oversight by Malta fund managers, coinciding with structural reforms under Act XV/2026 (new Regulatory Decisions Committee and Capital Markets Decisions Committee) strengthening enforcement independence.
findings.client_impact: HNW clients invested in Malta-domiciled AIFs or using Malta fund management structures should note that the MFSA is actively scrutinising outsourcing arrangements and has strengthened its enforcement machinery — fund managers that rely on outsourced administration or risk management should expect enhanced supervision and should proactively review their service provider oversight documentation.
findings.urgency_reason: No specific client-action deadline; background awareness for advisers with Malta fund exposure that regulatory scrutiny is elevated.

findings.title: Guernsey GFSC Q2 2026 Regulatory Update — Beneficial Ownership and Fund Manager Changes
findings.summary: Mourant's Q2 2026 Guernsey regulatory update covers GFSC consultation outcomes on fund manager authorisation, updated AML guidance, changes to the Private Investment Fund regime, revised beneficial ownership maintenance obligations, and capital requirements for smaller regulated firms. Cross-island AML/CFT mutual evaluation follow-up coordination with Jersey is noted.
findings.client_impact: Advisers managing Guernsey-based funds or SPVs for HNW clients should review the updated AML guidance and revised BO maintenance obligations to ensure ongoing compliance — while no urgent deadline applies, the mutual evaluation follow-up context means GFSC supervision of AML standards is likely to intensify through 2027.
findings.urgency_reason: General quarterly regulatory update with no specific imminent deadline; background awareness for advisers with Guernsey fund or BO register obligations.

jurisdictions_with_no_changes: Jersey (only finding filtered — JFSC Basel III Pillar 2 consultation is banking prudential regulation outside FGC wealth management practice areas)
